messages:
maria gonzalez: Quick proposal — we should define a compact, explicit ‘fallback_priority’ spec for canary/A-B rollouts so the runtime can make deterministic choices when capacity or region constraints hit. Thinking a 3-axis chain: model_variant -> region -> capacity_tier. What do folks think?

kevin choi: +1 on explicit chain. Need to clarify precedence and TTL for each fallback step. if a model_variant fallback is used for a request, do we sticky it for the session or request-only? :thinking_face:

julia wang: Agree we need session affinity opt-in. Default should be request-only for safety. We also need signal hooks so console/alerts can surface why a fallback happened (which leg and why).

samir patel: Drafted a tiny YAML for the API I had in mind: 
```yaml
fallback_priority:
  - kind: model_variant
    id: redwood/fast-l2q
    stickiness: request
    ttl: 0
  - kind: region
    id: eu-west-1
    stickiness: session
    ttl: 300 # seconds
  - kind: capacity_tier
    id: best-effort
    stickiness: request
    ttl: 0
fallback_budget: 0.02 # max fraction of canary traffic allowed to use any fallback
```

maria gonzalez: Nice. The fallback_budget is important — prevents noisy rollouts from silently routing everyone to cheap variants. We should define an emergency override for oncall with a higher budget and an audit log.

kevin choi: API semantics question: should fallback_budget be per-route or global per-rollout? Per-route gives fine-grain control but is a lot of knobs. Maybe default global, allow route-level override in rollout manifest.

julia wang: Console UX: show a small waterfall next to rollout chart: expected split vs actual split vs fallback split. Hover gets reasons and counts. Also a heatmap for which regions/tenants hit fallbacks.

samir patel: Telemetry we need: fallback_count, fallback_rate_by_leg, latency_delta_p50/p95_when_fallbacked, error_rate_after_fallback, rollback_trigger_score. We should surface these as chartable metrics and expose in alerts (SLOs degrade > X).

ops-bot: deploy-check: canary manifest validation passed (manifest 0.1.3). No quota conflicts detected.

maria gonzalez: Edge case: what if quota throttling and per-tenant limits cause fallback churn? We should add a cooldown per-tenant and a small randomized backoff to avoid oscillation.

kevin choi: Implementation note: runtime should prefer non-disruptive fallbacks first (model quantized variant) then cross-region only if the local region has exhausted capacity. capacity_tier fallback should be last and only when still under budget. Also add a debug header the runtime returns: X-Redwood-Fallback: model_variant=...,reason=cap-exhausted

julia wang: UX note: in rollout config modal, add a checkbox "Allow cross-region fallback" and a clear tooltip about data residency implications + a required approval step for private deployments.

samir patel: I'll spin up a quick POC in the runtime branch that implements the YAML and emits the metrics above. Will add e2e test that simulates node preemptions and region blackhole.

maria gonzalez: Great — please also add a unit for the budget enforcement (stateless sliding window) and a manual override path for oncall. cc @kevin for API review.

kevin choi: Review tomorrow. If we agree on naming and stickiness semantics I can add the API docs + SDK examples (curl + JS). Example curl: `curl -X POST /rollouts -d '{"fallback_priority":...}'`

maria gonzalez: :thumbsup: thanks — moving to action items.

deploy-bot: note: rollout 0.2 will include canary-fallback flags. Scheduled gate: 2025-04-03 17:00 UTC.
